pictures.scene: Church, Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives — the whole city seen across the valley from the olive hill at first light, a towering bank of cream and grey cloud piled up the left side of the sky and warm gold light spreading over the rest of it, the long city wall running right across the picture with its battlements and a dark arched gate, the temple platform behind it green with grass and planted trees, the great dome and its blue tiled drum standing in the middle of the roofs, a slender white minaret beside it and the pale domes and flat roofs of the whole town crowded away to the horizon, the deep Kidron valley below in shadowed olive and brown with a little white tomb on the slope and scattered olive trees in the hollow, a silvery olive tree hanging into the picture at the right, and at the bottom a stony white path coming up over the ridge with three small travellers on it throwing long morning shadows, one mounted on a camel, one walking beside it in a red cap and one in blue, and a lone figure further off up the track, but jesus went to the mount of olives, early in the morning he went back into the temple courts, …
pictures.name: pd_church_jerusalem_from_the_mount_of_olives

pictures.scene: Poussin, Christ and the Woman Taken in Adultery — the accused woman brought out into a stone square and the accusers answered, a strip of blue sky with thin cloud across the top and below it a town of grey ashlar walls, red-tiled roofs, a long flight of open steps, an arcade of round arches and a little potted shrub set on a ledge, Christ standing in the middle of the picture at full height in a scarlet cloak thrown over a deep blue tunic, his long auburn hair and short beard, his face turned to the accusers and his mouth open as he speaks, his right arm reaching out bare from the sleeve and one finger pointing straight down at the pavement, his bare foot showing at the hem, the woman sitting low at the left in a white shift and a wide blue skirt with a white cloth bound over her hair, her arms folded in against herself and her head dropped so that her face is turned down and away, a man in a short dark tunic standing behind her with a staff over his shoulder, two accusers crowding in at the right edge with their hands thrown open, one of them turning a startled face up toward us, a man in red cut off at the left edge, and a scatter of loose stones lying on the paving between them, in the law moses commanded us to stone such a woman, …
pictures.name: pd_poussin_christ_and_the_woman_taken_in_adultery

pictures.scene: Surikov, The Morning of the Streltsy Execution — condemned men carried out through a packed square at dawn to be put to death, the painted onion domes of a great cathedral rising across the whole top of the picture in green, blue and rust spirals with gilded crosses and tiers of arched brickwork, a grey morning sky showing in a narrow strip behind them, a low stone wall below with heads crowded along it and a man leaning over it to look, a thicket of halberds and pikes standing up out of the crowd, and in front a jam of rough carts with great wooden wheels sunk in the churned black mud, each cart carrying a condemned man in a white shirt with a lit candle burning in his fist, one at the left with his shirt open at the chest and his head bowed over the flame, one in the middle with a black beard and wild eyes staring straight out, a white-bearded old man at the right being held back by hands laid on him, an officer in a red coat and a cocked hat pressing in among them, a young woman in a red and white headcloth with her face screwed up crying, an old woman in black slumped forward on the ground in the middle of the picture with her hands hanging open between her knees, and a small girl in a scarlet kerchief standing beside her looking out at us with her mouth open, let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her, …
pictures.name: pd_surikov_the_morning_of_the_streltsy_execution

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Christ and the Woman Taken in Adultery — the accused woman kneeling on a pale stone step in the half dark of the temple, the great building going up behind into brown shadow with a tall gilded pier catching the light, a railed gallery high up crowded with small lit figures leaning out to watch, and a heavy brass column standing at the right, Christ at the left of the picture standing full height in a plain brown robe, his long reddish hair falling loose and his thin bearded face turned down toward her, his hands quietly together in front of him and his bare feet on the lit step, a tall accuser in a dark coat beside him with his beard thrust forward and one hand opened out as he puts the case, a priest behind him in a jewelled gold cap and a long embroidered stole, a row of heads crowding in behind them, two soldiers in steel breastplates with their halberds, the woman herself kneeling in the middle of the picture in a white gown and a gold chain with a long white veil hanging from her hair, her shoulders rounded and her head bent right down so that her face is almost hidden, and a man in gold stooping over her with his hand on her veil, until only jesus was left, with the woman standing there, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_woman_taken_in_adultery

pictures.scene: Memling, Christ Giving His Blessing — the face of Christ brought up close and filling almost the whole picture, painted smooth and pale against a deep blue-green ground with fine ruled gold rays running out from the head on either side, his long dark brown hair parted in the middle and falling in heavy waves down past his shoulders, a thin soft beard and moustache, the mouth closed and quiet, and the clear eyes looking straight out at whoever is standing in front of the panel, a plain dark red robe closed high at the throat, and one hand lifted up in front of his breast with the first two fingers raised and the others folded in, the nails and the knuckles painted one by one, and the tips of the other hand just showing at the bottom edge, then neither do i condemn you, jesus declared, now go and sin no more, …
pictures.name: pd_memling_christ_giving_his_blessing

pictures.scene: Hunt, The Light of the World — Christ standing alone at night outside a long-shut door with a lantern in his hand, a pale gold ring of light round his head and a crown of plaited thorns set over a jewelled gold crown on his dark hair, his bearded face turned quietly out toward us, a long white robe falling to his bare feet, a heavy scarlet cloak hanging from his shoulders and a stiff embroidered mantle over it clasped at the breast with a great jewelled morse, one arm raised at the left to knock on the weathered boards of the door, the door itself grown over with trailing ivy and tall dead weeds and never opened, brambles, nettles and yellowing leaves banked along the bottom of it, fallen apples lying in the wet grass, a wood of bare branches and a dark field behind him, and in his lowered hand a pierced iron lantern hung on a chain, the candle burning inside it and the light pushing out through the little windows and spilling red over the fold of his cloak, i am the light of the world, whoever follows me will never walk in the darkness, …
pictures.name: pd_hunt_the_light_of_the_world

pictures.scene: Friedrich, Morning in the Riesengebirge — the whole country seen from a mountain top at sunrise, the sky graded all the way up from a warm cream band on the horizon through pale rose into clear blue with a few long thin cloud streaks lying across it, range behind range of hills running back into the distance in lilac, violet and soft blue until they fade out altogether, a thick white sea of mist lying in the valleys below and breaking against the lower slopes, a dark heathery shoulder of moor at the left, and on the right a great crag of warm red-brown rock going up in broken ledges and splinters from the bottom of the picture to the summit, with a slender wooden cross planted on the very top catching the first light, and two small figures on the rock beside it, one in a long white dress reaching back with her hand held out to the other who is climbing up behind her, because i know where i came from and where i am going, …
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_morning_in_the_riesengebirge

pictures.scene: David, The Oath of the Horatii — an oath sworn between a father and his sons in the bare hall of a Roman house, two round-headed arches of worn brick and plaster going up across the top of the picture, heavy grey stone columns standing between them and a dark empty room beyond, and a floor of red herringbone tiles across the bottom, the old father standing at the right with his back half turned, his grey curling hair and beard, his face lifted and his mouth open as he speaks the words, a scarlet cloak hanging from his shoulder over a white tunic, his legs bare to the knee and his feet in plain sandals, and his raised fist holding up three naked swords with the blades spread out like a fan and one hand opened flat above them, the brothers stepping forward from the left in red cloaks, bronze helmets with crests and short tunics, their three arms thrown out straight and stiff together toward the swords with the hands flattened and the fingers taut, the first of them in a plumed helmet with his jaw set, and the blue and crimson folds of a seated woman's dress showing at the right edge, even in your own law it is written that the testimony of two men is valid, …
pictures.name: pd_david_the_oath_of_the_horatii

pictures.scene: Masaccio, The Tribute Money — Christ questioned in the open and answering with a lifted hand, bare brown tree trunks with thin branches going up across the top of the fresco against a pale grey sky and a hazy green hillside behind them, Christ standing a little left of the middle in a rose pink tunic with a deep blue cloak swung across his body and over his arm, a thin gold halo behind his auburn hair, his short beard and his eyes turned aside, his right hand reaching out with the first finger lifted and the other hand gathering the blue cloth at his hip, a grey bearded apostle pressing in at the left edge with a worn lined face, a bald wide browed apostle just behind Christ staring out with his mouth open, more haloed heads crowded along behind them to the right, and the tax collector standing in front of us in a short orange tunic belted at the waist, seen from behind with his bare legs and bare feet planted on the worked stone, one arm stretched out toward Christ and the other held back, a fair haired young man beside him turning away, and pale worked stone steps going up at the lower right, where is your father, they asked him, …
pictures.name: pd_masaccio_schatting

pictures.scene: Metsys, The Moneylender and His Wife — a man weighing money at a counting table with his wife beside him, a brown wooden shelf running right across the top of the panel carrying a pewter dish, a red apple, a rolled paper, a little carved box and two worn leather bound books laid on their sides, the dim boarded room behind them, the money changer sitting at the left in a dark fur trimmed hat and a brown gown, his long thin face bent down and his eyes lowered to his work, both hands lifted in front of him holding the slender beam of a pair of scales with a small weight hanging in one pan, the wife at the right in a brilliant scarlet gown with a grey fur collar and a stiff white linen headdress folded over her hair, her round young face turned down with him and her finger lifting the leaf of a painted and gilded prayer book open on the table, and spread out across the worn tabletop in front of them a scatter of gold and silver coins, pearls, a ring, a glass flask, little round weights, and a round convex mirror lying on its back and throwing back the cross barred window and the street outside, he spoke these words while teaching in the temple courts, near the treasury, …
pictures.name: pd_metsys_the_moneylender_and_his_wife

pictures.scene: Durer, The Vision of the Seven Candlesticks — a woodcut all in fine black lines on white, one figure enthroned high up in the clouds and another fallen down beneath him, banks of curling cloud piled along the top and down both sides with long ruled lines of sky between them, the enthroned figure sitting in the middle in heavy folded robes with a girdle across his breast, a great mane of curling hair and a long forked beard, a ring of straight rays shooting out all round his head, his face looking out with wide eyes, his right arm flung out to the left with seven many pointed stars held in his open hand, a long double edged sword laid across his face and running out past his shoulder, and an open book propped in his lap with two columns of lettering on its pages, tall branched candlesticks standing round him on twisted stems with lit candles burning in their sockets, two at the left, one in front and two more at the right, and in front of the throne an old man collapsed on the clouds on his hands and knees with his curling hair falling forward, his long robe crumpled in deep folds around him and his bare feet turned up behind, you are from below, i am from above, you are of this world, i am not of this world, …
pictures.name: pd_durer_the_vision_of_the_seven_candlesticks

pictures.scene: Bosch, Death and the Miser — a rich man still handling his money at the foot of his own deathbed, a tall pink curtained bed standing across the top of the panel with a dark pillar at the left and a pale limb hanging out of the bedclothes, a bent old man in a long olive green gown and a green wound cap standing at the right of the middle, his lined face in profile and his mouth half open, one hand dropping a gold coin into an open strongbox while the other grips a tall walking stick, a bunch of keys and a little purse hung at his belt, the heavy wooden chest in front of him with its great iron lock plate, its lid thrown back and a red bag of coins, a dagger and a cup inside it, a grey clawed demon crouched underneath pushing another coin in and a second one at the left holding up a sealed paper, lizard footed creatures crawling out from under the chest, a hooded devil with mottled wings peering over a stone ledge below, the man's cast off clothes left hanging over the ledge in pink and rust, and down on the ochre floor his abandoned armour, a steel helmet with its crest, a long lance laid across the boards and a rat slinking away at the corner, that is why i told you that you would die in your sins, …
pictures.name: pd_bosch_death_and_the_miser

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Saint Peter Preaching — an old apostle speaking out to a crowd in the open air, a soft green mountain rising across the whole upper half of the fresco with little dark trees dotted over its slopes and a bare plastered wall showing at the right where the painting breaks off, Peter standing at the left of the picture in a pale blue tunic with a heavy orange cloak hanging in deep folds to his bare feet, a thin gold halo behind his white hair and his short white beard, his face in profile and his mouth open as he speaks, his right hand lifted beside his head with the fingers raised, two men in blue gowns and round caps standing behind him, and packed in front of him a crowd of listeners, two women kneeling in the middle in deep blue and rose with their heads veiled and their faces turned up to him, a white bearded old man kneeling beside them with his head bowed low, rows of faces behind in caps and hoods looking up over one another, and at the right a group of friars in white and dark habits, one of them turning a lined old face out toward us, what i have heard from him, i tell the world, …
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_saint_peter_preaching

pictures.scene: Bellini, The Agony in the Garden — Christ kneeling alone on a bare hillside at daybreak and praying while his men sleep, a clear blue sky across the top with long banks of grey and rose cloud lying in it and a warm apricot light burning along the horizon, a flat green plain behind with a little walled town, a line of trees and a hill town up on the right, Christ kneeling in the middle of the picture facing away from us on a shelf of tawny rock, a deep blue cloak falling in heavy folds from his shoulders over a red tunic and a red sash, his brown curling hair, his face turned up in lost profile toward the sky and both hands raised and pressed together, his bare feet showing behind him, a sleeping apostle lying on the ground in the near corner wrapped in a rose pink cloak over a yellow robe, his grey bearded face tipped back and his mouth open and his sandalled feet stretched out, and far away at the left a long column of small soldiers winding along a track toward them with spears, round shields and helmets catching the light, he has not left me alone, because i always do what pleases him, …
pictures.name: pd_bellini_agony_in_the_garden

pictures.scene: Johnson, The Lord Is My Shepherd — a man sitting by himself in a dim room reading, the wall behind him worked in deep red brown with a plank door and its frame standing at the left edge, the upper part of the room going away into warm darkness, and a bare board floor across the bottom lit in gold, the man seated on a low stool near the middle of the picture, leaning forward with his elbows on his knees and his head bent right down over his hands, his dark hair, his cheekbone and his brow catching the light, a loose white shirt with the sleeves rolled up on his forearms, a dark waistcoat and a yellow neckcloth hanging open at his throat, dark trousers and heavy worn boots set flat on the boards, and in both hands an open book held low in his lap with the lamplight falling full on its pages, a bundle and a scatter of cloth lying on the floor at the right, if you continue in my word, you are truly my disciples, …
pictures.name: pd_johnson_the_lord_is_my_shepherd

pictures.scene: Ge, What Is Truth — a governor putting a question to a prisoner in a sunlit stone hall, a plain red brown plastered wall running across the whole upper part of the picture with a dark doorway cut into it at the left and a band of worked greenish stone panelling lower down, and a floor of pale honey and red tiles across the bottom with one broad slab of sunlight thrown across it and the long shadows of both men lying over it, the governor standing in front of us at the left with his back turned, a heavy ochre and olive toga wound round him down to his sandalled feet with a red border at the hem, his close cropped grey head seen in sharp profile, his mouth open and his bare right arm flung out with the palm turned up as he asks, and the prisoner standing at the right against the wall in deep shadow, upright and still in a long dark red robe with a worn cloak over it, his bare feet together on the tiles, his hands hidden, his tangled dark hair and beard round a thin worn face, and only his brow and his eyes catching the light as he looks quietly back, then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free, …
pictures.name: pd_ge_what_is_truth

pictures.scene: van Gogh, Prisoners Exercising — men tramping round and round a shut yard with no way out, high brick walls going up on every side and filling the whole upper half of the canvas, every brick laid in with a separate stroke of green, blue, ochre and rust, a corner where two walls meet running straight up the middle, three small barred and arched windows set high in the right hand wall and one in the left, no sky anywhere, and a cold grey green pavement below, the prisoners circling in a close ring in the bottom half in drab worn jackets and striped trousers, some with cropped heads and some in caps, one in front with a thin pale face and yellow hair looking straight out at us, the man beside him with his head down and his cap pulled low, the men at the left walking away from us with their hands clasped behind their backs and their shoulders rounded, the line bending round at the back and coming forward again, and three warders in dark coats and hats standing watching at the right hand edge, everyone who sins is a slave to sin, …
pictures.name: pd_gogh_gevangenisplaats

pictures.scene: Bierstadt, Sunrise in a Mountain Valley — a wide open valley filling with light at sunrise and nobody in it, a pale green blue sky across the top streaked with thin drawn out cloud, the whole middle of the picture flooded with warm gold haze where the sun is coming up behind the hills, a great grey cliff standing up at the left with its ledges and gullies catching the first light and its lower slopes lost in mist, blue ridges running back one behind another into the glare, two tall open branched trees leaning in from the right with their thin autumn leaves lit gold and their bare limbs drawn against the light, a flat still river winding across the bottom of the valley with the gold of the sky lying on the water, small bushy trees and scrub standing along its banks, and a dark foreground of broken rock and coarse brown grass in shadow running across the bottom of the picture with low boulders pushing up out of it, so if the son sets you free, you will be free indeed, …
pictures.name: pd_bierstadt_sunrise

pictures.scene: Flinck, Isaac Blessing Jacob — a blind old father laying his hand on the son who has come to him in his brother's place, the room behind them going up into brown darkness with a heavy curtain hanging in long folds down the middle, the old man propped in his bed at the right in a pale blue nightgown with a crimson fur trimmed robe laid over him and a dark blue cap on his head, his thin face tipped down, his eyes closed, his mouth open as he speaks the blessing, a great white beard spreading over his chest, one hand stretched right across the picture to rest on the young man's hair and the other laid flat on the white bedsheet, the son kneeling at the bed on the left with his curling brown hair, his young face turned up and sideways with a wary look in it, a goatskin tied over his neck and a loose scarf at his throat, an embroidered sleeve and a gloved hand resting on the bed, and the mother standing behind in a brown gown and a dark headcloth watching the two of them with her mouth set, a rust red coverlet falling over the foot of the bed, abraham is our father, they replied, …
pictures.name: pd_flinck_isaac_blessing_jacob

pictures.scene: King David Kneeling Before an Altar — a crowned king down on one knee praying, the brown panelled wall behind him hung with a heavy scarlet curtain looped back on a red cord with a thick tassel, an angel in white sweeping down out of a bank of grey cloud at the top left with a drawn sword held up in both hands, and a dim altar standing off in the shadow at the left, the king kneeling in the middle of the picture at full size, a jewelled gold crown set on his thick auburn hair, his bearded face lifted and turned up to the angel with his mouth open and his eyes wide, a white ruffed collar at his throat, a steel breastplate and a scarlet tunic underneath, and over it a great stiff cope of gold embroidery falling in broad panels to the floor with little scenes worked into medallions all over it, one bare foot showing under the hem, his right hand laid flat on his breast, his left hand reaching down to a golden harp propped against his knee, and at the right edge of the picture two hands holding an open book out toward him with lettering across both its pages, our only father is god himself, they declared, …
pictures.name: pd_king_david_kneeling_before_an_altar

pictures.scene: Hofmann, Christ and the Rich Young Ruler — two men standing close together against a plain dim stone wall, Christ at the left turned toward us in a rust red robe with a deep blue green cloak hanging from his shoulder and falling down the whole left side of the picture, his long brown hair, his short beard, a faint warm glow in the stonework behind his head, his face quiet and his eyes steady, and his right arm reaching away out of the picture at the left with the hand open and the fingers spread, the young man beside him at the right in a cream mantle with a gold embroidered border, a green silk undersleeve, a patterned sash and a richly wound turban with a jewelled clasp over his dark hair, his smooth young face seen in profile, his eyes lowered and his mouth closed, his hands held together low in front of him, and the two of them standing so near that his shoulder almost touches Christ's arm while he looks away at the ground, it is because you are unable to accept my message, …
pictures.name: pd_hofmann_christ_and_the_rich_young_ruler

pictures.scene: Bermejo, Saint Michael Triumphant over the Devil — the archangel standing over the devil with his sword raised, a burnished gold ground worked all over with scrolling patterns filling the whole back of the panel, the angel at full height in the middle of the picture in gleaming gilt plate armour from his gorget down to his pointed steel shoes, a mail skirt and sleeves showing underneath, a green sash round his waist, his smooth young face framed in fair curling hair and tipped calmly to one side, his eyes lowered to the thing under his feet, great wings of orange, red and dark green spread open behind him, a stiff crimson cloak of embroidered and jewelled silk blowing out in angular folds across the whole upper left of the panel, his right arm stretched up above his head gripping a long sword by the hilt, and his left hand low at his side holding a round crystal shield by its gold rim, under his feet a scaly reptile devil sprawled across the ground with a shaggy black horned head, glaring red eyes, a wide open mouth full of pointed teeth, clawed limbs, a second red eye set in its back and a long coiling tail, and at the left a donor kneeling small in a grey brocade gown and a tall black cap with an open book in his hands, looking up at the angel, you belong to your father, the devil, …
pictures.name: pd_bermejo_saint_michael_triumphant_over_the_devil

pictures.scene: Dou, Old Woman Reading a Lectionary — one old woman alone with a book, the room behind her nothing but warm olive brown shadow, her head and shoulders filling the right side of the picture and turned in profile, a fur cap pushed back on her head with a wide pale linen band wound round her brow, thin grey hair showing under it, her forehead, her cheek and her long nose brightly lit, her eyelids lowered and her lips pressed together, every wrinkle of her face and throat painted one by one, a heavy dark gown with a broad brown fur collar and a little gold and garnet brooch pinned at her breast, and held up close in both her hands a big open book, its thick worn pages catching the light, two columns of black gothic lettering on them with a red initial and a small printed picture set into the text, and her knotted fingers hooked over the edge of the paper, whoever belongs to god hears the words of god, …
pictures.name: pd_dou_old_woman_reading_a_lectionary

pictures.scene: Duccio, Christ and the Samaritan Woman — a stranger from Samaria talking with Christ at a well, a worn gold ground scratched and rubbed with age filling the whole upper part of the little panel and a corner of pale building showing at the right edge, a six sided well standing in the middle built of green marble with a white stone rim and set on a wide pale stone platform with steps running round it, Christ sitting on the rim at the left in a rust red tunic under a deep blue cloak edged with gold, a fine gold halo ruled behind his dark hair, his thin bearded face turned toward her and his right hand lifted and open as he speaks, his other hand resting flat on the stone and his bare feet set on the step, the woman standing across the well from him in a long pale cream dress with a white veil over her hair and an earthenware water jar balanced on her head, one hand raised toward him with the palm out and the other holding the rope and bucket hanging at her side, her face turned to him and her brows drawn together, and at the left edge the dark cloaks of men standing just outside the picture, are we not right to say that you are a samaritan, …
pictures.name: pd_duccio_christ_and_the_samaritan_woman

pictures.scene: Angeli, Elijah Taken Up in a Chariot of Fire — an old prophet carried up off the earth alive, a pale grey blue sky across the top of the canvas, a huge billow of peach and orange flame boiling up under him and filling the whole middle and lower half of the picture, and far below at the bottom a dark headland, a flat sheet of grey water and a low bright horizon, the prophet himself filling the picture seen from underneath and swept upward, his bald head and his long white beard turned back over his shoulder and his eyes looking up, a heavy fawn coloured robe wrapped round him with the sleeves falling back from his wrists, a great white mantle blowing loose across his lap and down out of the flame in deep folds, both his hands gripping the cloth, his bare feet showing at the bottom of the robe, and at the right edge the broad gilded wheel of a chariot with its thick spokes turning up out of the fire beside him, if anyone keeps my word, he will never see death, …
pictures.name: pd_angeli_elijah_taken_up_in_a_chariot_of_fire

pictures.scene: Ruisdael, The Jewish Cemetery — a burial ground of old stone tombs lying under the walls of a ruined church, a heavy grey and white storm cloud banked across the top of the picture with a faint rainbow breaking through at the left and two small birds crossing it, the roofless church standing in the middle in warm tawny stone with its empty window arches and broken gable open to the sky and a second ruined choir further off to the right, dark green oaks and a wind bent tree growing up around the walls, two tiny dark figures standing among the graves, and in the whole lower half of the picture a great fallen tree trunk split and barkless across the ground, rough grass and brambles, three white and pale blue marble tomb chests with their lids cracked, flat slabs sunk in the earth, and a shallow stream running white over stones along the bottom edge, abraham died, and so did the prophets, …
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_the_jewish_cemetery

pictures.scene: Guercino, God the Father — an ancient figure shown from the waist up and filling the whole picture, seen against a plain warm salmon coloured ground with a wide soft halo of pale light glowing all round His head, His face bent down and turned a little to one side, the brow and cheek strongly lit and deeply lined, the eyes lowered under heavy lids, a great mass of loose grey and brown hair blown back from the temples and a long thick white beard spreading down over the breast, a deep scarlet cope clasped at the throat with an embroidered band and falling open over a white shirt and a golden brown robe, the sleeves heavy and shadowed, a pale violet lining showing at the edge of the mantle, and a bank of soft grey cloud gathered under Him along the bottom of the canvas, the one who glorifies me is my father, …
pictures.name: pd_guercino_god_the_father

pictures.scene: Exner, Grandfather — a very old countryman standing in the middle of a low beamed cottage room and laughing quietly to himself as he looks down at the floor, a knitted cap pushed back on his white hair, a short white beard on his chin, a dark coat worn open over a buttoned waistcoat and a striped neckcloth, wide loose breeches gathered below the knee, pale stockings and heavy wooden clogs on his feet, a little pipe and its chain held down in one hand, a young granddaughter standing at the left in a kerchief and a long grey apron with a ball of white wool and her knitting in her hands and her eyes lowered to her work, behind them a dark carved cupboard crowded with pewter and a lidded tankard on a scrubbed table, a small looking glass and a painted corner cabinet on the pale wall, a doorway open at the far left, and across the whole bottom of the picture a lit bare plank floor where a hen and her chicks are pecking, your father abraham rejoiced that he would see my day, …
pictures.name: pd_exner_grootvader

pictures.scene: Cole, The Departure — a company riding away out of a castle and down into an open valley, a pale blue morning sky streaked with thin cloud across the top of the picture, a high grey peak and a long range of hazy mountains behind with a thin white waterfall falling from the cliffs, the castle itself standing on the wooded height in warm brown stone with round towers, battlements, a tall keep and a pennon flying, a long arched viaduct carrying the road out from its gate, below that a second gate tower on a stone bridge over a stream where a line of small riders with lances and a big banner is filing across and down the road, dark oaks and massed green woods on both sides, a bright sunlit meadow in front with a few goats lying under a great tree, and at the very bottom a lone bearded man in a long brown habit standing on the track with a staff and a palm branch, his hand raised toward the riders, but jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area, …
pictures.name: pd_cole_the_departure

lines.text: But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives. Early in the morning He went back into the temple courts. All the people came to Him, and He sat down to teach them.
The scribes and Pharisees, however, brought to Him a woman caught in adultery. They made her stand before them
and said, Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of adultery.
In the Law Moses commanded us to stone such a woman. So what do You say?
They said this to test Him, in order to have a basis for accusing Him. But Jesus bent down and began to write on the ground with His finger.
When they continued to question Him, He straightened up and said to them, Let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her.
And again He bent down and wrote on the ground.
When they heard this, they began to go away one by one, beginning with the older ones, until only Jesus was left, with the woman standing there.
Then Jesus straightened up and asked her, Woman, where are your accusers? Has no one condemned you?
No one, Lord, she answered. Then neither do I condemn you, Jesus declared. Now go and sin no more.
Once again, Jesus spoke to the people and said, I am the light of the world. Whoever follows Me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.
So the Pharisees said to Him, You are testifying about Yourself; Your testimony is not valid.
Jesus replied, Even if I testify about Myself, My testimony is valid, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I came from or where I am going.
You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.
But even if I do judge, My judgment is true, because I am not alone; I am with the Father who sent Me.
Even in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two men is valid.
I am One who testifies about Myself, and the Father, who sent Me, also testifies about Me.
Where is Your Father? they asked Him. You do not know Me or My Father, Jesus answered. If you knew Me, you would know My Father as well.
He spoke these words while teaching in the temple courts, near the treasury. Yet no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet come.
Again He said to them, I am going away, and you will look for Me, but you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.
So the Jews began to ask, Will He kill Himself, since He says, Where I am going, you cannot come?
Then He told them, You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world.
That is why I told you that you would die in your sins. For unless you believe that I am He, you will die in your sins.
Who are You? they asked. Just what I have been telling you from the beginning, Jesus replied.
I have much to say about you and much to judge. But the One who sent Me is truthful, and what I have heard from Him, I tell the world.
They did not understand that He was telling them about the Father.
So Jesus said, When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He, and that I do nothing on My own, but speak exactly what the Father has taught Me.
He who sent Me is with Me. He has not left Me alone, because I always do what pleases Him.
As Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him.
So He said to the Jews who had believed Him, If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples.
Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.
We are Abraham's descendants, they answered. We have never been slaves to anyone. How can You say we will be set free?
Jesus replied, Truly, truly, I tell you, everyone who sins is a slave to sin.
A slave is not a permanent member of the family, but a son belongs to it forever.
So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.
I know you are Abraham's descendants, but you are trying to kill Me because My word has no place within you.
I speak of what I have seen in the presence of the Father, and you do what you have heard from your father.
Abraham is our father, they replied. If you were children of Abraham, said Jesus, you would do the works of Abraham.
But now you are trying to kill Me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham never did such a thing.
You are doing the works of your father. We are not illegitimate children, they declared. Our only Father is God Himself.
Jesus said to them, If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I have come here from God. I have not come on My own, but He sent Me.
Why do you not understand what I am saying? It is because you are unable to accept My message.

You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me!
Which of you can prove Me guilty of sin? If I speak the truth, why do you not believe Me?
Whoever belongs to God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear is that you do not belong to God.
The Jews answered Him, Are we not right to say that You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?
I do not have a demon, Jesus replied, but I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me.
I do not seek My own glory. There is One who seeks it, and He is the Judge.
Truly, truly, I tell you, if anyone keeps My word, he will never see death.
Now we know that You have a demon! declared the Jews. Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet You say that anyone who keeps Your word will never taste death.
Are You greater than our father Abraham? He died, as did the prophets. Who do You claim to be?
Jesus answered, If I glorify Myself, My glory means nothing. The One who glorifies Me is My Father, of whom you say He is our God.
You do not know Him, but I know Him. If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know Him, and I keep His word.
Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see My day. He saw it and was glad.
Then the Jews said to Him, You are not yet fifty years old, and You have seen Abraham?
Truly, truly, I tell you, Jesus declared, before Abraham was born, I am!
At this, they picked up stones to throw at Him. But Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area.
